Finding and baseline source
Required correction and evidence




Overlapping docs/output/cache paths; docs . or ancestor; symlinked parents; separator-bearing labels. yml.rs:337, clear.rs:158, fs_utils.rs:1.
Reject unsafe destructive destinations before writes; resolve identity/overlap and staging aliases; protect source/raw/root state. External resource paths remain valid. Test actual preservation with root/ancestor/overlap/traversal/symlink fixtures.

Public docs cleared before ignored promotion failures; post-cleanup precedes CAS export. build.rs:359, build.rs:370, build.rs:430.

Environment read errors suppressed through lines().flatten(); invalid names can panic; required files can be ignored. env.rs:69, env.rs:181.
Bounded reads, validation before mutation, explicit errors for directory/unreadable/empty/NUL inputs; prove analysis never starts.

Validate early; prefer supported renderer controls, otherwise exact-byte restoration on every exit.

One validated destination and explicit supported format mapping; reject unsupported formats rather than guessing; require actual expected artifacts.

Pass data/arguments to fixed R code; test spaces, apostrophes, backslashes and Unicode without local R execution.


Remote paths stay invocation-relative and invalid content tags/errors are dropped. yml.rs:429, build.rs:435.
Normalize paths against the captured root, validate content tags before writes and propagate export failures.


CAS path normalization can collide on Unix; scan/copy race can store bytes under the wrong digest. cas.rs:202, cas.rs:248.
Preserve platform path distinctions or reject unsupported names; verify stored bytes against digest and fail on source mutation.


CAS broader integrity gaps: existing-object trust, unsafe boundaries, non-atomic manifest, CSV escaping, existence-only verification, malformed digest/path traversal and missing/file source accepted as empty snapshot.
Extend existing CAS work rather than claim a redesign is complete. Require a real input directory and fixture-backed integrity/error behavior.


Unsupported control keys silently filtered; runtime invents directory defaults/subpaths. yml.rs filtering/validation/get_path.
Enforce approved active configuration and explicit used mappings, reject unsupported behavior settings before mutations. Init alone may write defaults.






After bounded configuration fixes: destructive-path guards; complete managed-state failure/promotion handling; per-run environment; Git authentication/operation corrections; exact path/context behavior; explicit renderer checks. Managed-state restoration cannot undo arbitrary external effects of user scripts or hooks. This is not an OS sandbox or global rollback promise. No trustworthy production-release safety claim follows from preview tests or this static audit. The existing R package and thesis remain untouched.

title: proj ignore
text:
Commands for interacting with tracking file exclusions, handling operations to manually or automatically modify .gitignore and .Rbuildignore files.


Manually appends one or more raw file or directory paths to the project ignore files.
Unlike automatic configurations driven by _proj.yml, these manual entries represent permanent, user-specified exclusions and are placed strictly above the # --- PROJ MANAGED --- blocks.



<PATHS>...: One or more raw file or directory paths to be ignored.
--force-create: Boolean flag (default true). If true, creates ignore files if they don’t exist. If false, skips file creation unless inherently warranted by environmental cues (e.g. finding a .git folder or a DESCRIPTION file).
--type: Optional filter selection (all [default], git, rbuild). Determines which tracking surface receives the manual path entries. Note that .Rbuildignore is skipped entirely if no DESCRIPTION file exists at the project root.





Manually forces paths to be tracked by appending negated syntax (e.g. !path/ or ^!pattern$).
These unignore entries represent permanent, user-specified negations and are placed strictly below the # --- END PROJ MANAGED --- boundary in .gitignore and .Rbuildignore files.



<PATHS>...: One or more raw file or directory paths to force tracking.
--type: Optional filter selection (all [default], git, rbuild). Determines which tracking surface receives the negated entries. Note that .Rbuildignore is skipped entirely if no DESCRIPTION file exists at the project root.





The library core automatically synchronizes ignore rules dynamically across .gitignore and .Rbuildignore based on the configuration of _proj.yml.

Note: While the automated ignore synchronization is invoked implicitly by the CLI via commands like proj yml read (and acts seamlessly under the hood), the ignore subcommand namespace exists openly to support explicit manual additions via proj ignore add.




The tool automatically locates the project boundaries via a heuristic upward path traversal. It begins checking from the user’s current working directory upward: - It discovers the conceptual root by finding a directory containing a VERSION file. - It continues upward through up to 5 directory levels seeking an optimal foundational root confirming the presence of either _proj.yml or a .git tracking context alongside the VERSION.



The tool targets specifically two core exception list files: - .gitignore (safeguards git commit environments) - .Rbuildignore (safeguards strict CRAN environments and rbuild processes)
Based on the individual block ignore settings within _proj.yml (e.g. ignore: all), properties are intelligently resolved as standard git glob patterns and Rbuild regex match patterns appropriately.



Modifications made by the tool into .gitignore and .Rbuildignore are safely strictly demarcated with protected slice logic block comments. This preserves user-defined modifications outside the managed span: - Operations scan for # --- PROJ MANAGED --- and # --- END PROJ MANAGED ---. - Targeted slice elements are swapped or appended into existing scopes only between these exact markers. - If the boundary blocks are absent, the tool automatically injects them natively at the base end.

title: proj build
text:
The build pipeline script execution engine for the project.
This command evaluates what files need to be run based on configuration layout parameters (build.scripts in _proj.yml) or filesystem auto-discovery. It sorts them according to strict engine precedence rules, modifies format-specific configuration templates when necessary, and executes each script inside its own independent, isolated subprocess.



--major, --minor, --patch: Specifies the version bump strategy for a production build.
--profile: An optional profile to configure execution context.
--description: An optional description string for the build commit. If omitted during a production build that involves git commits, the CLI will interactively prompt for a one-line description when running inside a valid terminal session.





Pre-flight Dependency Checks: Before modifying files or triggering git snapshots, the build engine statically resolves targets to identify dependencies. Depending on the matched scripts (such as .Rmd, .qmd, or .py) and configuration files, it asserts the availability of Rscript (verifying required R namespaces like rmarkdown or bookdown), quarto, or python executable commands. Any missing R packages can be resolved automatically via the PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL environment variable, or through an interactive terminal prompt.
Production Build Restrictions: Checks if branch rules (only_branches, not_branches) or upstream synchronicity (not_behind) are violated during a production build run.
Remote Export Pipeline: During the post-build phase, conditionally exports resolved local target outputs into a deduplicated Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) vault as defined via build.dest targets in remotes.local.
System Git Provider Abstracted: Git mutations safely resolve through a strictly encapsulated host System Git adapter, securely avoiding hanging inputs and ensuring older systems correctly push mutations.
Mutual Exclusion Checking: Before executing, proj build checks for project-level configurations (_quarto.yml and _bookdown.yml). If both exist and the build targets include Quarto or RMarkdown documents, it throws an error to prevent conflicting rendering.
Explicit Execution (Path A):

Define exact scripts, exclusions (starting with !), or sub-directory globs in _proj.yml under build.scripts.
Can rewrite _quarto.yml or _bookdown.yml configuration if specific subset documents are requested.
Maintains order relative to Python and R scripts, while correctly clustering and executing project documents together.

Fallback Execution (Path B):

If no build.scripts is provided, the engine auto-discovers build targets.
Will execute a Quarto project if _quarto.yml exists, or a Bookdown project if _bookdown.yml exists.
Otherwise, it falls back to a shallow workspace sweep and runs .qmd, .Rmd, .R, and .py files in that strict order.





Every resolved file or project rendering task runs inside its own completely independent subprocess, isolated via environment profiles (PROJR_PROFILE) and correct working directory assignments (current_dir), preventing memory leaks and state pollution across execution runs.



proj build-dev
Development runs execute the existing script selection with development Git settings disabled. The CLI does not create or update VERSION, update ignore files, clear released output or previous caches, promote rendered documents into docs, or export to configured local archives. These rules apply on success and failure, even when production configuration enables cleanup, commits or export.
Scripts should explicitly write preview artefacts into their declared cache or staging locations. A subprocess is not a filesystem sandbox: scripts, hooks and renderers can still write where their own code/configuration directs them. Renderer configuration rewriting and script working-directory behavior retain their existing semantics. This change does not introduce automatic output redirection, recursive discovery or a new project-root policy.



build.scripts: [] selects no analysis scripts. Hooks still run, and production builds can version and export existing artefacts as an upload-only workflow. Analysis cleanup, renderer setup and document promotion are skipped so those existing artefacts are preserved. The CLI does not discover scripts instead.
For previews, an absent dev.scripts inherits build.scripts; dev.scripts: [] overrides it with no analysis. Hooks still run, but previews never publish.



Builds require root-level _proj.yml, legacy _projr.yml, or an explicitly activated _projr-<profile>.yml. Inactive profiles and _projr-local.yml alone do not qualify. Both base filenames together are an error. Unsupported control fields fail before build writes; arbitrary parameters and metadata maps are allowed. Configuration errors include their causes on stderr and return failure.
This validation is separate from project discovery. A root marker or cwd fallback does not make an unconfigured project buildable. Explicit directory enforcement, per-run environment isolation and complete managed-state failure restoration remain under development; see the behavior contract and pinned legacy audit.
Explicit script/hook include patterns must match at least one file. Use an empty list (scripts: []) when intentionally selecting no analysis; unmatched configured includes return an error instead of a successful no-op.

title: Command exit status
text:
Successful CLI commands return exit status zero. Reported operation failures return a nonzero status and a diagnostic on stderr, including configuration/path queries, version reads/writes, ignore updates and initialization. Argument parsing errors also return nonzero.
For example, a malformed _proj.yml makes proj yml read --project demo fail, so a shell or frontend can stop instead of treating the diagnostic as success. Failed Git staging, commits and GitHub creation propagate as initialization errors; a failed remote inspection does not proceed to GitHub creation.
This defines success versus failure, not stable error codes, a JSON result schema or a capability protocol. Diagnostics remain human-readable text. Commands may perform work before failing; a nonzero status is not a rollback guarantee.


proj build-dev --project demo --non-interactive
--non-interactive disables the CLI’s own prompts and automatic R-package installation, including when PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL=true. Missing dependencies produce an error. Script, hook and renderer runners and controlled R dependency probes receive closed stdin. The mode is inherited by managed children as PROJ_NON_INTERACTIVE=true.
Initialization still performs requested operations using its existing defaults. This flag does not choose project markers, change configuration precedence or define a structured result protocol. Third-party code remains responsible for its own behavior after receiving EOF.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
WarningTry it on a disposable project



Use sample data or a disposable copy of your project. Production builds (proj build) can modify or remove files, and safety fixes are still pending. Never run production builds on the only copy of important work. Previews are not a security sandbox; code you run can still change files.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
1. Make a small project
In an Ubuntu terminal, choose a new folder and open it:
mkdir projcli-example
cd projcli-example
Create a file named _proj.yml with this content:
directories:
  raw-data:
    path: _raw_data
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  output:
    path: _output
build:
  scripts: [analysis.py]
The paths are explicit: runtime does not supply missing mappings or invent undeclared labels.








Label
Folder
Role in this example




raw-data
_raw_data
Input files; unused because our three measurements are built into the script.


cache
_tmp
Temporary results; the script writes inside _tmp/preview.


output
_output
Result files; unused by this preview.



Only cache is used by this Python example. The other two mappings match the local initializer’s preset. No docs path is implied: document rendering needs an explicit docs mapping too.
The explicit build.scripts list selects our one script. No Git setup, remote repository or initialization command is needed for this manual setup.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
2. Add an analysis
Create analysis.py in the same folder:
import csv
import os
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import mean

root = Path(os.environ["PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT"])
preview = root / "_tmp" / "preview"
preview.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

measurements = [10, 12, 14]
result = preview / "summary.csv"
with result.open("w", newline="") as handle:
    writer = csv.writer(handle)
    writer.writerow(["count", "mean"])
    writer.writerow([len(measurements), mean(measurements)])

print(f"Saved {result}")
The three measurements are deliberately built into the script so there is no data download or extra package installation. The script uses the project root provided by projcli and explicitly writes to _tmp/preview.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
3. Check, then run
proj --project . yml read
proj --project . --non-interactive build-dev
cat _tmp/preview/summary.csv
The CSV should contain:
count,mean
3,12
The validation command reads configuration. The preview runs the script. Running it again replaces this example’s CSV; change a measurement and rerun to see the mean change.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
4. Understand what changed
The script creates _tmp/preview/summary.csv. The CLI does not create a VERSION file, publish to docs, or export an archive during this preview.
A preview is not a sandbox: your script can still write elsewhere if you tell it to. Keep preview writes in an explicit temporary folder.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
Starting another project
In another new project folder, local-only directory setup is available:
proj --project . --non-interactive init directories
When no base or active profile configuration exists, this writes _proj.yml with the explicit raw-data: _raw_data, cache: _tmp and output: _output paths, creates those folders, and updates ignore files. It does not run Git or GitHub setup. Existing configuration files are preserved; only their declared directories are created.
The generated file omits build.scripts, allowing the normal shallow script discovery. To choose an exact analysis, add a scripts list as above. An explicit scripts: [] selects no analysis scripts; hooks can still run. Initialization does not turn an absent scripts key into an empty list.

text:

Query a declared path with proj --project . path get --label cache.
Add your own script to build.scripts.
Read the build reference before using proj build. Production builds have different version, cleanup and export behavior.
Check what works before adding document rendering or R tooling.

title: Project and execution behavior
text:
This is the product behavior contract. Confirmed decisions below guide implementation; they are not claims that the current CLI already implements them. Proposals require review before they become requirements. The compatibility log records pinned projr comparisons, decisions, actual test evidence, Ponytail reviews and remaining gaps; update it with each PR.



A project is one analysis/build unit anchored at a selected root directory. It has settings, version information and named resource paths where applicable. Resource paths may be outside the root; a project need not be a Git repository.

title: Configuration _proj.yml
text:
The _proj.yml file dictates the structural map of your project. It configures the foundational paths and mapping logic used by the CLI.


Custom directory labels are strictly validated against a set of foundational prefixes: - cache - raw - output - docs
These prefixes are case-insensitive. Any label defined in the configuration must begin with one of these approved identifiers.



Every declared directory needs a nonempty path. Runtime does not insert missing cache/raw/output/docs mappings or synthesize subpaths for undeclared labels. For example, declaring raw-data: {path: _raw_data} makes raw-data available; it does not create an undeclared raw or raw-data-extra resource. ASCII case is ignored and case-only duplicate labels are rejected.
proj --project . --non-interactive init directories creates a missing _proj.yml once with explicit raw-data: _raw_data, cache: _tmp, and output: _output paths. It preserves existing base/profile files, creates only declared resource directories, and does not invoke Git/GitHub or add an R code directory. The preset omits build.scripts, preserving shallow discovery; it never serializes an accidental empty analysis list. To render documents, declare a docs mapping too.
Production state and project-render staging require a declared cache directory. Framework version/staging children are derived inside that declared cache; this is distinct from inventing undeclared resource labels. Storage content labels must be declared and relative storage paths use the captured project root.



The system performs strict validation on _proj.yml: - If a defined directory label uses an unsupported prefix layout, a validation error string will be returned and execution will fail. - All references must resolve correctly; otherwise, the CLI will output an error detailing the structurally invalid labels or malformed content.



The _proj.yml file supports a top-level config block for project-wide settings:

config.git.engine: The Git execution engine to use. Can be auto (default) or system. This determines how the CLI interfaces with Git capabilities natively.
config.git.use_proj_cred_helper: Defaults to false: use existing native Git authentication. Explicit true permits an existing single-line GITHUB_PAT, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN for standard HTTPS github.com remotes through a temporary host-scoped helper. There is no automatic token discovery or GitHub CLI call during builds. Tokens are environment data, never argv or shell source; persistent auth settings are unchanged.




The _proj.yml file supports a top-level parameters block for arbitrary nested parameter evaluation. This allows you to define custom metadata and deeply queried values throughout your execution environment.
The configuration engine also supports several aliases for this block: parameter, params, and param. However, multiple alias conflicts within the same configuration file are structurally rejected during validation to prevent mapping confusion.



The _proj.yml file supports a top-level remotes block, which currently supports a local mapping of standalone storage vaults.

local: A mapping where keys represent remote titles and values configure the vault:

path: The physical absolute or relative path to the remote storage directory.
structure: Specifies the storage structure algorithm. Must be cas (Content-Addressable Storage).
content: An array of string tags (matching foundational prefixes or defined directories) specifying which project output directories to sync into the remote upon build completion.
inspect: manifest validates JSON, logical paths/digests and manifest filename/content identity; file additionally hashes every referenced object and compares actual bytes. Manifest-only inspection does not verify object bytes.





The _proj.yml file can also contain a build block to configure the behavior of the proj build and proj build-dev execution engine. The build block supports the following sub-keys:

dest: An optional list of remote target strings. These targets must be mapped to explicit configurations within the remotes.local block. During post-build execution, resolved content directories matching these tags are piped to the CAS engine for deduplicated storage synchronization.
scripts: An optional list of explicit script paths or glob patterns to execute during the build pipeline.

Globbing patterns are supported.
Prefix a pattern with ! to exclude matching files from execution.
When provided, this selects scripts instead of automatic discovery. Document targets may be grouped for rendering, so mixed script and document targets are not guaranteed to run in the exact listed order.

hooks: An optional map of lifecycle hook scripts to execute.

pre: Scripts executed before the actual build phase.
post: Scripts executed after analysis/promotion, before VERSION and publication.
both: Scripts executed during both pre and post phases.

profile: An optional environment profile identifier. When set, the system injects the PROJR_PROFILE environment variable into the isolated subprocess for all executed scripts and project rendering commands. This can be overridden at runtime via the --profile CLI flag.
git: An optional Git integration configuration. This can be a boolean toggle or an object mapping out detailed toggles:

commit: Defaults to false, including inside an existing Git repository. Explicit true requires initially clean Git state and commits once after successful local build; an unchanged staged index is a successful no-op.
push: Defaults to false. Explicit true publishes HEAD to the current branch’s configured upstream remote/reference. Missing upstream or custom push-only routing fails before build writes; origin/main is never invented.

restrictions: Configuration block to enforce Git checks specifically during production builds:

only_branches: A list of allowed branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is not in this list.
not_branches: A list of restricted branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is in this list.
not_behind: Omitted/false performs no fetch. Explicit true fetches the current configured upstream and compares its state. If enabled, production builds will verify that the local branch has an upstream tracking remote and is not behind it, aborting if the local branch needs to pull upstream changes.

clear_output: An optional string controlling workspace clearing routines for output directories. Can be set to "pre", "post", or "never". If omitted, defaults to evaluating the PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT environment variable.




You can define a dev block to completely override specific configurations during development builds (proj build-dev).

scripts: A list of script paths or globs. During development builds, this array entirely overrides build.scripts. An explicitly empty array ([]) selects no analysis scripts. An absent dev.scripts inherits build.scripts. Hooks can still run.
hooks: A mapping identical to build.hooks. When specified, these completely replace build.hooks during a development build.
old_dev_remove: Retained configuration field. The current preview protections skip CLI cleanup of prior caches during development builds, even when this is true. Scripts and hooks still control their own writes.





PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL: During the proj build pre-flight checks, if required R packages (like bookdown or rmarkdown) are missing, this environment variable controls remediation. If set to true, packages are automatically installed. If absent or set to false, the tool defaults to an interactive terminal prompt (if available) or fails hard.

The configuration engine also supports several aliases for this block: parameter, params, and param. However, multiple alias conflicts within the same configuration file are structurally rejected during validation to prevent mapping confusion.

title: Configuration _proj.yml
text:
The _proj.yml file supports a top-level remotes block, which currently supports a local mapping of standalone storage vaults.

local: A mapping where keys represent remote titles and values configure the vault:

path: The physical absolute or relative path to the remote storage directory.
structure: Specifies the storage structure algorithm. Must be cas (Content-Addressable Storage).
content: An array of string tags (matching foundational prefixes or defined directories) specifying which project output directories to sync into the remote upon build completion.
inspect: manifest validates JSON, logical paths/digests and manifest filename/content identity; file additionally hashes every referenced object and compares actual bytes. Manifest-only inspection does not verify object bytes.

title: Configuration _proj.yml
text:
The _proj.yml file can also contain a build block to configure the behavior of the proj build and proj build-dev execution engine. The build block supports the following sub-keys:

dest: An optional list of remote target strings. These targets must be mapped to explicit configurations within the remotes.local block. During post-build execution, resolved content directories matching these tags are piped to the CAS engine for deduplicated storage synchronization.
scripts: An optional list of explicit script paths or glob patterns to execute during the build pipeline.

Globbing patterns are supported.
Prefix a pattern with ! to exclude matching files from execution.
When provided, this selects scripts instead of automatic discovery. Document targets may be grouped for rendering, so mixed script and document targets are not guaranteed to run in the exact listed order.

hooks: An optional map of lifecycle hook scripts to execute.

pre: Scripts executed before the actual build phase.
post: Scripts executed after analysis/promotion, before VERSION and publication.
both: Scripts executed during both pre and post phases.

profile: An optional environment profile identifier. When set, the system injects the PROJR_PROFILE environment variable into the isolated subprocess for all executed scripts and project rendering commands. This can be overridden at runtime via the --profile CLI flag.
git: An optional Git integration configuration. This can be a boolean toggle or an object mapping out detailed toggles:

commit: Defaults to false, including inside an existing Git repository. Explicit true requires initially clean Git state and commits once after successful local build; an unchanged staged index is a successful no-op.
push: Defaults to false. Explicit true publishes HEAD to the current branch’s configured upstream remote/reference. Missing upstream or custom push-only routing fails before build writes; origin/main is never invented.

restrictions: Configuration block to enforce Git checks specifically during production builds:

only_branches: A list of allowed branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is not in this list.
not_branches: A list of restricted branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is in this list.
not_behind: Omitted/false performs no fetch. Explicit true fetches the current configured upstream and compares its state. If enabled, production builds will verify that the local branch has an upstream tracking remote and is not behind it, aborting if the local branch needs to pull upstream changes.

clear_output: An optional string controlling workspace clearing routines for output directories. Can be set to "pre", "post", or "never". If omitted, defaults to evaluating the PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT environment variable.

title: Configuration _proj.yml
text:
You can define a dev block to completely override specific configurations during development builds (proj build-dev).

scripts: A list of script paths or globs. During development builds, this array entirely overrides build.scripts. An explicitly empty array ([]) selects no analysis scripts. An absent dev.scripts inherits build.scripts. Hooks can still run.
hooks: A mapping identical to build.hooks. When specified, these completely replace build.hooks during a development build.
old_dev_remove: Retained configuration field. The current preview protections skip CLI cleanup of prior caches during development builds, even when this is true. Scripts and hooks still control their own writes.

title: Configuration _proj.yml
text: PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL: During the proj build pre-flight checks, if required R packages (like bookdown or rmarkdown) are missing, this environment variable controls remediation. If set to true, packages are automatically installed. If absent or set to false, the tool defaults to an interactive terminal prompt (if available) or fails hard.

title: What works
text:
On main: development preview
These capabilities are implemented on main. They are not a claim about the older published package.







Capability
What it means for you




Choose the project
--project PATH selects the folder for a command. Child queries retain that root.


Preview an analysis
build-dev runs your selected steps without CLI version changes, output promotion or archive export.


Read without changing files
Configuration validation and path queries do not create target folders or edit ignore files.


Detect command failures
Errors produce a nonzero exit status, so an automated run can stop.


Run without questions
--non-interactive disables CLI prompts and automatic package installation, and closes runner input.


Select no analysis
An explicit scripts: [] runs no analysis scripts. Hooks may still run; production can export existing outputs.


Run scripts and render documents
The build engine supports Python, R, Quarto and R Markdown/Bookdown targets, with the corresponding tools installed.


Keep a local output archive
Production builds can export configured outputs to local content-addressed storage, which avoids storing identical content repeatedly.




Preview has a boundary
The CLI skips its own release operations during a preview, including cleanup of released outputs and prior caches. This is not a filesystem sandbox. Scripts, hooks and renderers can still change files. Write preview results to an explicitly chosen temporary folder, as in the tutorial.
Document renderers have their own working folders and output rules. Mixed-language scheduling is not a promise that every target runs in the exact order written in configuration. See the build reference for the current implementation and the behavior contract for limits.

title: Build execution flow
text:
This describes the current Rust implementation, not a complete correctness or reproducibility guarantee. The behavior contract records approved semantics and the compatibility log records evidence and gaps.


Capture the project root, resolve a private per-run environment without changing the parent process, require active root configuration, and merge base/profile/local settings. Validate fields, explicit directory paths, targets, hooks and destructive destinations. Explicit empty scripts select no analysis. Otherwise explicit globs or shallow root discovery select inputs; project rendering may use its own input discovery. Explicit Python-only selection does not activate an unused Quarto/Bookdown project marker.
Read VERSION with DESCRIPTION/default fallbacks. Check selected interpreters and configured Git restrictions before controlled project writes. Existing preflight can still invoke Git/network checks or R package remediation; these are known limitations, not a clean-environment guarantee.



Before authoritative writes, capture exact bytes, permissions and presence/absence for the managed set documented in the compatibility log. This includes VERSION, ignore/configuration files, existing root regular files, selected in-project inputs, declared output/docs trees and planned individual rendering artifacts. External declared output/docs directories are allowed. Linked managed trees are rejected. Backups stream into private OS temporary storage outside disposable project cache. Backup creation failure prevents authoritative project writes.
One local error/panic boundary covers ignore synchronization, requested pre-cleanup, pre/both hooks, script/document execution, renderer configuration, promotion and post/both hooks. Required output promotion errors propagate. Renderer configuration is restored exactly, retaining comments and originally absent keys. Candidate version changes stay in memory; VERSION is written only after those stages succeed. No pre-build Git commit is created.
On local failure, restore the captured managed set, including originally absent files/directories. Attempt all restorations; retain recovery backups and report both the primary and restoration errors when recovery fails. This does not undo arbitrary script effects outside the captured set or provide a filesystem sandbox, power-loss atomicity or protection against concurrent filesystem replacement.



Storage export and Git publication start after successful local completion. Export actual declared content before requested clear_output: post cleanup. Create one configured final Git commit, then push when enabled. A publication or later cleanup failure reports that local analysis succeeded and retains its release/version; external publication is not rolled back.
Git upstream/authentication policy, stable attempt/release records and an analysis-free publication retry command remain unfinished. Push uses the captured current-branch upstream; custom push-only routing remains unsupported and fails before authoritative writes. Native authentication is the default.



Previews skip production version changes, cleanup, commits and exports. They run selected hooks/analysis and restore renderer configuration bytes. Cooperating scripts must choose appropriate output locations; preview is not automatic output isolation or an OS sandbox. Script/hook subprocesses start in the captured root. Quarto receives an explicit execution directory and individual R Markdown receives knit_root_dir. Direct R/IDE renderer parity remains unfinished and is not established by these CLI controls. The existing R package remains untouched.

title: Machine interface
text:
Machine interface
Use proj --machine <command> for automation. Human command output remains the default. proj capabilities (also with --machine) reports protocol/capability versions and supported command families without loading a project.
Protocol version 1 writes one JSON object and a newline to stdout. Both success and failure include protocol_version, cli_version, ok, result, and error. result is null on failure; error is null on success. Failures exit nonzero. Broken output pipes cannot receive a complete object and also exit nonzero.
proj --machine capabilities
proj --machine --project . path get --label output
proj --machine --project . version get
proj --machine --project . yml read
proj --machine --project . build-dev
Successful queries return { "path": "..." }, { "version": { "major": 1, "minor": 2, "patch": 3, "dev": 0 }, "text": "v1.2.3" }, or { "validated": true }. Configuration queries validate without returning raw configuration or parameter values. Other existing command families reuse the ordinary CLI in a noninteractive subprocess and return { "completed": true } only when that command succeeds. Unsupported command arguments fail; capability flags explicitly report absent preview isolation, attempt/release records and direct R/IDE parity.
Stable error codes are invalid_arguments, project_selection_failed, query_failed, command_failed, and worker_unavailable. Messages are static; raw config, environment values, command arguments and chained domain errors are not copied into protocol errors. This transport reuses existing anyhow domain handling tracked by issue87; it does not promise a finer domain-error taxonomy. With --machine, help/version display requests return capability negotiation.
All command progress and child stdout/stderr go to stderr, streamed directly without accumulating logs in memory. Machine mode closes child stdin and enables noninteractive policy. Child logs are user/third-party output and are not a secret redaction service; avoid printing credentials in scripts. No environment/config dump is included in the machine result. Callers must keep stdout and stderr separate.
A failed publication can follow successful local analysis. command_failed is not a rollback or retry instruction: inspect local state/diagnostics before retrying. No analysis-free publication retry or successful release record is invented here.

Relationship: follows projr’s merged-configuration intent and the approved local > earlier profiles > later profiles > base precedence. The prior Rust pipeline validated merged settings but separately reread the base for execution.
Implemented: deserialize and validate one merged value, then select scripts and hooks from it. Explicit empty dev selection remains empty; absence falls back to build settings. Both base filenames use this same execution path. Configuration parsing/validation, target resolution and preflight now precede production environment-ignore writes.

Remote CI and independent review pending; no real R/renderer execution is claimed.

The 2026-10-20 static audit records the pinned baseline, reported failure paths, required regressions and correction order. Its findings are not runtime reproductions or completed fixes. Highest managed-state risks remain blockers to production-safety claims; arbitrary external script effects are outside managed rollback. No mechanical edition upgrade or CAS redesign is claimed. This review uses the actual Ponytail full-mode skill to prioritize root causes and data-preservation checks over cosmetic rewriting.




Relationship: deliberate difference from projr convenience defaults, as explicitly approved. Every build requires a base file or activated profile; inactive profile/local files alone do not qualify. Discovery still falls back to cwd independently. Empty analysis is valid with active configuration.
Implemented: build gate before writes; unsupported typed configuration fields fail instead of disappearing in a top-level filter. Build failures include their error causes so unsupported-field diagnostics name the field. Arbitrary parameter and metadata maps remain supported and parameter aliases reach validation.
Evidence: runnable tests cover active/base/legacy/inactive/local/no-config cases, unsupported nested keys, dynamic maps and no pre-build state writes. Remote CI/independent review pending. Explicit directory enforcement is still a separate gap; this does not yet establish transaction/promotion safety.
Ponytail full-mode review: reused Serde’s unknown-field validation and the existing active profile resolver; removed silent filtering from runtime reads. No new parser/schema/dependency. Kept the old public filter helper only for compatibility; runtime no longer uses it.

PR134 merged-context evidence: exact head 29b2bdfb564f3193a0e93eb43096f89f2691653a passed all nine checks in runs 39490264159/39490264169. Independent review inspected the three new regressions across platforms and cleared the bounded change. Merged as eb1204026e8809780fc783f27b0be7edf9b5033e. Canonicalize the one accepted alias to parameters in the shared reader before merging. New fixtures cover all 64 base/profile/local alias combinations, earlier-profile precedence and retained nested values; same-file multiple aliases and YAML duplicate keys remain errors. Ponytail full-mode re-review kept the fix at the shared loader, without caller guards or a second merge model. Exact amended CI/re-review remain required.




Relationship: new safety checks, not a blanket ban on external resources. Before production analysis cleanup, reject root/ancestor destinations, staging and resource overlaps, selected-input containment, VCS metadata, label path separators and symlinked managed-write paths. Directory replacement also requires an existing source and disjoint destination before deleting bytes.
Evidence: runnable preservation fixtures cover root, ancestor, staging, raw/output overlaps, traversal labels, Unix symlink parents and low-level self/ancestor/nested/missing-source moves. Remote CI/review pending.
Limits: does not yet provide atomic promotion or complete rollback, protect against concurrent hostile filesystem replacement, undo user-script external effects or establish full CAS integrity. External disjoint paths remain valid.
Ponytail full-mode review: one stdlib identity resolver shared by build and promotion guards; trace all promotion callers, retain explicit errors instead of silently accepting missing source/read errors. No new dependency.

Path-guard Ponytail re-review traced the public cleanup helpers as well as build: direct clear_pre/clear_post now apply the shared destination checks, clear_old rejects symlinked staging parents, and traversal-bearing version components fail before cache deletion. Label separator validation lives in shared typed validation for all modes. Generic destructive move APIs require resolved parents and reject symlink aliases; positive direct-API fixtures canonicalize their temporary roots so macOS system temp aliases do not violate that explicit safety precondition. Added a direct-cleanup preservation fixture. This is not complete transactional restoration or a guarantee against concurrent filesystem replacement.
PR135 final evidence (batched with path guards): code head 3839173366e55cffa946ea0e2afe4757ae48e77d passed all alias/conflict regressions on three platforms and independent re-review. Base-update head abc62f966766915093351c00a6a1724a0d1b69da changed no executable/tests/Cargo code, preserved the published site, passed all ten checks in runs 39492001512/39492001479/39492001493 and focused independent review. Merged as a0909e413915847498e77669a3b669941dbfe3fe. Required active config and unsupported field rejection are implemented; explicit used-directory enforcement and finite control-value validation remain separate gaps.
PR137 independent review found that configured-root checks alone missed derived version/output cache leaves. Validate all actual cleanup bases before the first deletion, including configured-cache and legacy staging paths. Direct dev cleanup is now a true no-op. The same review traced individual document promotion and recursive copying: validate paths before creating directories or renaming files, require actual outputs, reject traversal/aliasing and prevalidate asset moves. The two duplicate individual-renderer helpers now reuse one guarded implementation. Added targeted direct-API regressions; amended remote CI/re-review are required. This does not yet fix build callers discarding promotion errors or provide full restoration/atomicity; those remain the following focused work.
The repaired PR137 guard prevalidates concrete generated-file/asset paths and both legacy/configured cache-derived leaves before VERSION/ignore writes, including dangling links. Individual and project promotion now resolve the configured docs destination rather than a root/docs fallback; Python-only builds do not clear unrelated docs. Unix fake-Quarto/fake-R CLI fixtures exercise the reported linked root/docs sentinel bypass and actual successful external promotion, without a real renderer installation. Direct helper tests remain cross-platform.
Project-render source safety is explicitly conservative: recognized source-like .qmd, .Rmd, .md and .ipynb files or links in managed cleanup trees cause an early error. This can reject generated Markdown there; it is not exact Quarto or Bookdown input discovery. Keep sources and managed destinations separate until a renderer-provided input plan is supported. Quarto’s documented project input types are described in Project Basics.
The prepared literal-root glob fix is included in PR137 because a metacharacter root otherwise hides explicit inputs from the cleanup containment guard. Reuse glob::Pattern::escape for the root prefix only, retaining user include/exclude syntax. Runnable tests verify actual analysis bytes and selected-input preservation under a bracket-containing root. This is the same audited root-cause fix, not an additional discovery policy or dependency. Existing standalone preparation remains preserved and must not later be merged as duplicate work.
Windows CI at 9938173 exposed a skipped explicit failing script. Source review of glob 0.3.3 confirmed that escaping the canonical Windows namespace changes its filesystem prefix. Normalize Disk/UNC namespaces for glob transport only, keep filesystem prefixes literal, escape only directory components and join patterns using native path operations. The captured root is unchanged. Explicit include patterns with no files now fail instead of reporting successful no-op execution. New native/canonical-root execution markers run on every platform; network UNC execution remains unverified.
The same review found generated filenames could overwrite another selected script or hook, DESCRIPTION or environment configuration. Before renderer invocation, compare all concrete output/asset paths against the complete selected-input set and reject authoritative project/environment metadata filenames. Fake-renderer fixtures prove those failures happen before scripts, VERSION or ignore writes. Amended exact-head CI and independent re-review remain required.



Different (approved): runtime directory resolution requires declared nonempty paths and never invents missing labels or suffix subpaths. This supersedes earlier in-memory directory-default behavior, including read-only path queries. Missing configuration can still be queried as an empty inventory; builds require active configuration. Storage content labels must exist, and relative storage locations resolve against the captured root. Selected cleanup and project-render staging require cache; upload-only empty analysis does not require an unused cache mapping. Rendered documentation requires docs. Cache cleanup uses the declared mapping, not a parallel hard-coded _tmp tree.
Same preset / different timing: pinned projr 3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d, R/yml-dir.R:334–345, supplies raw-data: _raw_data, cache: _tmp, output: _output. Rust local-only proj --project . --non-interactive init directories writes those explicit paths once when no base/active profile exists. Existing configuration stays byte-for-byte intact. No scripts field is generated: absence preserves discovery, while an existing explicit empty list stays empty. No Git/GitHub/R setup is invoked. The Rust accepted label-prefix subset still differs from projr’s broader labels; this slice does not claim full schema parity or R frontend changes.
Ponytail full-mode review reused the shared resolver and existing tempfile dependency rather than adding a directory framework. Existing malformed/unreadable config preservation tests remain; new tests cover missing paths, undeclared labels, case collisions, explicit storage references, cache ownership, no-executable local init, preserved base/legacy/profile bytes and actual default-discovered Python output. Remote CI and independent review are pending. Init is not an atomic transaction against filesystem failures or concurrent replacement.
PR137 final eb727912f2f0302d01611cca7b84188d34c34e82 independently cleared; all ten checks passed (runs 39496127892/39496127915/39496127894). Merge 56564b9a4aeeef03ae199b04140b5f3d325b3505 passed post-merge test and installation runs 39496869636/39496869586 and published the site in 39496869590.
Independent PR139 review removed an over-broad production cache prerequisite. Only selected operations that consume cache require its mapping. Explicit empty analysis can export declared existing results without cache/docs mappings. An explicit Python-only selection does not activate a renderer merely because its project marker exists. The custom-cache fixture now executes Python and checks actual custom staging cleanup plus preserved legacy _tmp bytes. Fake-R fixtures declare docs while retaining EOF/no-install assertions. These amendments require fresh remote checks and exact-head re-review.



Same precedence / deliberate error handling difference: inherited OS values win over local, earlier environment profiles, then base assignments. Preserve non-Unicode inherited values rather than treating them as absent. Reject empty, equals-containing or NUL keys and NUL values before calling OS mutation APIs. Read whole files with propagated errors rather than lines().flatten(); required file errors and directory inputs cannot silently bypass validation or loop. Diagnostics include paths/line numbers, never assignment values. Same-file validation finishes before assignments from that file are applied. Ignore writes in explicit activation occur only after validation succeeds.
Ponytail full-mode review traced all load/assignment callers and reused existing configuration-entry presence checks. No parser dependency was added. Prepared CLI checks cover invalid/NUL entries, directory and permission-denied required files, secret-free diagnostics, actual inherited/local/profile/base child values and no analysis invocation on errors. Remote checks/review are pending.
This bounded fix does not make EnvGuard thread-safe: process-global environment mutation remains a known risk until per-run values and profiles reach all child commands and Git/preflight consumers. No credential handling or CAS code changes. ## Prepared managed-state restoration invariant (not yet verified)
The restoration implementation under preparation replaces the legacy middle-only catch and synthesized development-version rollback. Before controlled production mutations, capture exact bytes, permissions and absence for VERSION, ignore files, root configuration/state and existing root regular files; selected in-project inputs; declared output/docs directory trees; and concrete individual renderer output/asset paths. Capture initially absent parent directories too. Declared external output/docs paths are supported. Raw data, Git internals, arbitrary external user-script effects and cache contents are not backed up. Managed trees containing symlinks or unsupported entries are rejected rather than followed.
Backups use existing tempfile and streaming std::fs copies in private OS temporary recovery storage outside disposable project cache. No project mapping is invented, and cache-free upload-only operations remain supported. Recovery sources are copied to temporary restore staging before any current target is removed. Missing recovery bytes leave intact current state alone and are reported as unavailable.
One local failure boundary covers ignore synchronization, cleanup, all pre/both/ post hooks, engine configuration, execution, output promotion and VERSION writing. Promotion errors propagate; renderer configuration is restored byte-for-byte on success and failure. VERSION changes only after hooks/render/promotion succeed. Failures and caught panics restore captured state. All restore entries are attempted; if restoration fails, retain recovery bytes and report both the original failure and restoration failures with the backup path. Substituted links are rejected.
After local success, storage export/Git publication form a separate failure phase: publication failure reports successful local analysis and retains the new local release. Export precedes requested post-output cleanup so archives contain actual build bytes. A failure during this later cleanup is explicitly reported as such; there is no external publication rollback. No pre-build Git snapshot or second post-build commit is needed. Upstream selection/native credentials and publication retry identity remain separate unfinished work.
Prepared checks cover each hook/analysis failure, initially absent VERSION, exact old output/docs bytes and empty directories, renderer execution/missing promotion, exact YAML comments/render lists, restore-failure backup retention with external sentinels, and successful local analysis followed by failed storage publication. These are unrun: no local compilation under memory pressure; remote CI and independent review are still required. No power-loss atomicity, concurrent-writer or global script-side-effect guarantee is claimed. M2 attempt/release records and analysis-free retry commands remain open.
PR141 review corrections: normalize selected-input identities before comparing root containment (including Windows namespace forms); require nonempty supported document artifacts before project promotion; remove prior expected individual artifacts and project staging immediately before rendering. New regressions cover nested scripts/hooks modifying or deleting themselves, empty renderer staging, stale individual artifacts, cache purge during failed analysis, and unavailable recovery bytes without further deletion. These amendments require fresh remote CI and independent review. Project artifact scanning remains a conservative supported-document check, not a complete renderer manifest guarantee.
Further review keeps project promotion conservative: require a freshly created tree containing a nonempty supported document, rather than guessing per-input filenames from incomplete document-only format metadata. Fake PDF rendering tests cover explicit and inherited project formats. Complete expected-output manifests remain unimplemented; individual document format inference is still a separate known limitation. Selected managed script/hook paths reject symlinks along the original path before canonical identity comparison. System recovery temp anchors are canonicalized, including cache-free operations, without weakening user-path symlink rejection.
Bookdown’s framework-controlled <book_filename>_files source/destination are resolved and guarded before writes, with default _main and portable custom stems. Their exact prior bytes/presence join the recovery set. A fake successful render followed by a failing post-hook checks both default/custom native asset trees and released docs are restored. Unsupported path-like stems fail instead of traversing outside the project. Remote verification and independent review remain required.



Deliberate implementation change: build_project resolves inherited OS values, explicit profiles, local/earlier-profile/base environment files and required keys without modifying std::env. The same immutable context drives YAML profile selection, clear-output/installation/interaction controls, interpreter dependency probes, scripts/hooks/renderers and existing Git capability/preflight/publication commands. Child commands receive a captured environment, with the resolved project root and intentional script profile values applied per command. Inherited non-Unicode values remain intact. Existing Git credential selection/policy is forwarded, not redesigned.
Prepared remote checks force two library builds with different roots, profiles and fixture values to overlap while an unrelated child observes the unchanged parent. Mock R and Git commands verify probes and execution receive file-supplied values. Existing input/preflight/preview/root-context tests remain. Ponytail full-mode review reuses shared parsers and the standard Command.env_clear/envs API, with no global mutex or new dependency. No credentials are formatted through Debug or diagnostics. Remote CI and independent review are pending.
Legacy public EnvGuard activation/assignment APIs and CLI startup guards still mutate process state and are explicitly not safe concurrent environment APIs. The guarantee is bounded to the build path and commands receiving this context; unrelated external code that concurrently mutates std::env remains outside it. Native Git authentication/upstream policy and broader environment sanitization are separate unfinished work. R package and CAS code are unchanged.
PR143 Windows review correction: inherited native keys/values are passed through, but non-ASCII assignment/required keys in environment files are rejected early with a precise diagnostic. This deliberately bounded support avoids approximating Windows Unicode case identity and allowing a file alias to override an inherited key. ASCII case precedence and native non-Unicode values retain their dedicated platform tests. Unicode alias rejection is tested on Windows before analysis or authoritative writes; complete Unicode assignment-key support is not claimed.



Different/new, approved root policy: relative to pinned projr 3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d (R/engine.R, R/path.R) and the audited Rust script-parent cwd, scripts/hooks now start in the captured root. Shallow default enumeration and explicitly selected nested paths are preserved. Quarto uses its supported --execute-dir; individual R Markdown supplies knit_root_dir. R Markdown filenames are trailing data arguments to fixed R code, avoiding apostrophe/source interpolation. See Rscript arguments, rmarkdown render, and Quarto render controls.
Different/new, conservative supported subset: native R Markdown output and Quarto format select one known format; PDF/Word no longer guess HTML. Unknown or multiple formats, individual inherited metadata/unsupported output layouts, document-rendering hooks and nested Quarto roots fail early. This deliberately rejects previously guessed/unsafe layouts rather than claiming full renderer support. clear_output and ignore choices are finite early-validated values. No R production code changes, direct IDE verification or automatic preview isolation are included.
Ponytail full-mode review traced execution/preflight/promotion callers and reused existing YAML, command/environment and path safety facilities without new dependencies. Remote regressions are prepared for real nested Python hook/script ordering and cwd, safe R argument transport, HTML/PDF/Word promotion, nested roots, invalid controls and unsupported layouts preserving config/VERSION. CI and independent review are pending. PR144 exact head 344bddc4b82eb810b339e475eeb6824b1ef56bac passed independent review and all ten checks; merged 6c0079fb78b4f3f84df50423dae81c4b4a0e0f16 and post-merge workflows 39508879381/39508879332/39508879482 passed. Git clearance is bounded optional publication, not a complete release-readiness guarantee.



Different/new: the audited Rust baseline scanned/hash-named files, reopened them for copy, trusted existing objects, normalized Unix literal backslashes into slashes, accepted missing/file sources as empty snapshots and treated manifest existence as verification. This slice rejects missing/non-directory sources and unsafe overlap, linked/unsupported entries, ambiguous logical paths and malformed/non-ASCII digests before unsafe lookup. Literal backslash names are rejected rather than conflated with nested paths. Original source bytes are read only.
Hash the exact stream copied into temporary storage; validate existing object bytes before trusting the digest key. Immutable objects/manifests publish without clobber; manifest conflicts fail instead of truncating existing bytes. Manifest inspection parses/validates JSON and filename hash; file inspection hashes referenced objects. Index replacement uses complete staged bytes with CSV escaping for label/version. Temp fixtures use canonical physical paths so macOS system temp aliases do not silently weaken user-controlled symlink checks.
Ponytail full-mode review reuses BLAKE3, tempfile, shared path guards and standard streaming I/O. No new dependency or CAS schema/version-identity redesign. Prepared remote checks cover malformed paths/digests, Unix backslash collisions, missing/file sources, corrupt existing objects, changed source paths during stream copy, injected read errors, immutable manifest conflict and index failure with old state preserved, CSV metadata escaping and actual referenced-object hashes. Existing empty-directory and dedup/version-sensitive manifest tests remain. Remote CI/review are pending.
This advances existing MiguelRodo/issues#688–690 rather than creating duplicate roadmap issues. Broader CAS lifecycle/GC, a consistent concurrent-source snapshot, multi-writer index updates and crash durability remain open. Failed index publication may leave a complete unindexed manifest; object residue is valid but not a successful indexed export. There is no full cross-filesystem metadata transaction or global scientific reproducibility guarantee. Existing R package remains untouched.
PR145 review adds shared manifest file/directory prefix-collision validation. Logical files a and a/b cannot coexist, independent of input order or intervening names. Both inspection strategies are tested with real digest-matching objects so the rejection proves layout validation, not an unrelated missing-object failure.
CAS metadata readers/writers require regular files before reading existing manifest or index bytes; Unix named-pipe regressions use a bounded completion check so hostile special metadata cannot block verification or ingestion indefinitely.



Different/new (approved explicit-action policy): no commit/fetch/push/token requirement is inferred from Git metadata. Omitted commits and not_behind checks are off; explicit actions use the per-run environment. Commit builds fail before writes when Git already contains changes, preserving unrelated work; staged-index no-op is success. Publish one HEAD refspec to the configured current upstream, never origin/main. Custom pushRemote/pushDefault/remote.push routing is conservatively rejected early rather than silently choosing the wrong destination. Local release success remains distinct from publication failure. The retained reference projr and legacy Rust are evidence, not authority for these newer confirmed decisions.
Native Git authentication is default. Explicit use_proj_cred_helper enables only existing single-line environment tokens on standard HTTPS github.com remotes; no build calls GitHub CLI token discovery. Fixed helper code accepts only HTTPS github.com credential requests; the token is quoted environment data, not argv or shell source. The helper list resets for that one command; no persistent config or credentials are created. Captured network failures report status without reflecting potential secret stderr. Other hosts use native configured authentication. See Git’s credential helper protocol and upstream/refspec documentation.
Ponytail full-mode review reuses native Git, existing providers and shared environment context. No new dependency or credential store. Prepared remote checks use fake Git/GH to cover zero implicit calls, configured fetch only, real upstream/refspec, no-op/single commit, dirty-input preservation, native versus opt-in helper behavior, host/protocol denial, punctuation as literal token data, helper reset and secret-free argv/diagnostics. No real network/auth action is tested. Remote CI and independent review are pending; CAS integrity and analysis-free publication retries remain open.
PR143 reviewer note: the shared Windows ASCII assignment restriction also applies to public legacy EnvGuard::track_and_set, not just file-based keys. Inherited native environment values remain preserved; the legacy mutation APIs remain outside the build-path concurrency guarantee.
PR144 review guards force untracked-file and submodule visibility during the clean check, reject pushurl and multiple effective push URLs before writes, and disable follow-tags/submodule recursion for the single explicit push. Extra destinations are also checked at dispatch. Git’s executable is resolved explicitly from the per-run PATH (git.exe on Windows), avoiding native parent-PATH fallback in both availability checks and execution. Remote fixtures cover hidden untracked content, fan-out/redirection rejection and explicit suppression flags. Fresh exact-head checks and independent re-review are required.
The same preflight also rejects mirror pushes, absent remotes, multiple tracking merge entries and effective push/fetch endpoint differences (including expanded pushInsteadOf). Destination inspection uses get-url –push –all before controlled build writes. Native Git configuration is read only; no remote/auth settings are rewritten. Fake regressions assert each unsupported case preserves VERSION and unrelated private bytes and never reaches add/commit/fetch/push.
Captured push identity includes checked-out branch, upstream remote/ref and expanded effective endpoint, without Debug exposure. Revalidate the complete supported identity immediately before commit and again before push. Hook/script changes to URL, pushurl, mirror, branch, ref or remote fail publication without redirecting the push; successful local VERSION/output are retained. Fake regressions switch those values after an analysis marker and assert no add/commit/push occurs. This guards within-run mutation, not an atomic lock against concurrent external Git changes.
The sibling public post_build_sync API now uses the same captured-context checked publication helper as build_project. A fake commit hook changing the endpoint is rejected before push. Explicit Git lookup anchors directories absolutely but preserves the candidate leaf spelling, supporting symlink-based name dispatchers; a fake git-to-dispatcher symlink regression prevents argv[0] canonicalization regressions.



New: protocol-v1 opt-in JSON envelope and capability version, with static structured failure codes/nonzero exits. Existing human CLI remains default. Queries use explicit-root typed APIs rather than stripping progress prose; config validation returns no raw parameter values. Other command families reuse the existing CLI/domain paths in a noninteractive worker, redirecting child stdout and stderr directly to stderr without log buffering. No credentials/config/argv are copied into protocol errors. User/third-party logs are not auto-redacted.
Pinned projr 3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d is the workflow reference; this machine transport is a new language-neutral boundary, not established R API compatibility. No R code changes, finer domain-error taxonomy, release record or publication-retry semantics. Existing anyhow handling remains the domain layer; issue87 is not duplicated by a cross-module error rewrite.
Ponytail full-mode review uses existing clap/serde/anyhow/query/CLI facilities, standard subprocess stream redirection and no new dependencies. Prepared remote tests cover capability negotiation, typed queries without prose/secrets, malformed config/arguments/root, missing interpreter, child failure/logs, local init and version mutation. CI/independent review pending. Managed preview output isolation remains outstanding and is advertised as false, not described as sandboxing.
PR145 re-cleared CAS head 79050b3a46749a561b5a0cf0cca0451ae5532c6e passed all ten checks and merged 0e10b3e66face673fe966ed61b1be6d2eabf5004; post-merge workflows 39510143656/39510143483/39510143388 passed. CAS multi-writer/crash limits remain as previously recorded.
PR147 reviewer regression preserves the CLI option terminator and literal option-like positional values. Worker controls are inserted before --, and only actual machine flags before that boundary are removed; user paths/option values are retained.
PR146 review additionally rejects document/format-specific output extension and library-directory overrides before writes; these are outside the modeled artifact and recovery layout. Windows execution-root fixtures compare filesystem identity, preserving the cwd requirement across ordinary/verbatim path spellings.
Effective ancestor Quarto projects are rejected when they differ from an explicitly selected inner proj root. Every selected document routed through Quarto, including Rmd, receives nested-root validation. Metadata traversal normalizes root/input filesystem identity before stopping, avoiding Windows namespace spelling differences.
Retained Markdown (keep_md / keep-md, including format options) is rejected in individual layouts before rendering. A nested Rmd sibling sentinel regression with an overwrite-capable fake renderer and failing post-hook prevents this untracked framework artifact from damaging existing Markdown outside the recovery plan.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: unverified runtime parity; same documented intent. The R README and thesis design describe development previews separately from publication. This is evidence of intent, not proof that every R development path is inert.
Decision/rationale: keep CLI-managed release/version/archive changes out of previews so researchers can inspect development results without publishing.
Implemented: PR123, merged 5d145293e596c5797e9620bd3f00978fa6f99411; Dev-gated VERSION writes, cleanup, document promotion, local export and ignore updates in build.rs, env.rs and yml.rs.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: new explicit contract; renderer parity unverified. R path.R dynamically discovers a root, while the thesis defines the project workflow.
Decision/rationale: current approved behavior supersedes defects and stale architecture claims. Root/path defaults must agree across projr, quarto::quarto_render() and RStudio QMD Render. Quarto root equals proj root; nested Quarto projects are unsupported. Direct rendering does not imply release lifecycle parity; R Markdown Knit is a separate entrypoint.
Implemented: PR124, merged 635aa9efac0d7a28971236ab78c879b21be5ec31, corrected AGENTS/README/flow guidance and added the behavior contract. This was documentation, not renderer code.
Executed evidence: independent document review and remote Rust CI passed at dbf8d5fd94a87bba32ffc95cd2ee3b47f1e04277.
Gaps: no direct R frontend, Quarto/RStudio GUI or fresh-render-session parity test was performed. No projr production code or thesis text was changed.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: different root-resolution mechanism; new CLI selection. R path.R calls root discovery from current context. The CLI now captures one absolute root and passes it to each managed child as PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT.
Decision/rationale: explicit selection wins, and path queries must not change projects after cwd changes. This deliberately improves unstable root behavior rather than copying it.
Implemented: PR125, merged f265eb46c91a300fe0aafad3119d998038946a0b; project.rs, ignore.rs, main.rs and build.rs. Direct library builds configure each child command instead of mutating the caller’s process-global root.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at 779b3010040eeb23f08434478e0812173eb2a723 cover explicit precedence, spaces, invalid roots, changed cwd and overlapping builds in two distinct roots.
Gaps: marker discovery was not changed; R path helpers and direct render entrypoints do not yet consume this captured context. The tests do not promise general environment isolation or same-project concurrent builds.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: same static read-only configuration intent; runtime R parity unverified. R yml.R reads/merges configuration; this does not establish equivalence of every R public path helper or its cache routing.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Same precedence / deliberate error handling difference: inherited OS values win over local, earlier environment profiles, then base assignments. Preserve non-Unicode inherited values rather than treating them as absent. Reject empty, equals-containing or NUL keys and NUL values before calling OS mutation APIs. Read whole files with propagated errors rather than lines().flatten(); required file errors and directory inputs cannot silently bypass validation or loop. Diagnostics include paths/line numbers, never assignment values. Same-file validation finishes before assignments from that file are applied. Ignore writes in explicit activation occur only after validation succeeds.
Ponytail full-mode review traced all load/assignment callers and reused existing configuration-entry presence checks. No parser dependency was added. Prepared CLI checks cover invalid/NUL entries, directory and permission-denied required files, secret-free diagnostics, actual inherited/local/profile/base child values and no analysis invocation on errors. Remote checks/review are pending.
This bounded fix does not make EnvGuard thread-safe: process-global environment mutation remains a known risk until per-run values and profiles reach all child commands and Git/preflight consumers. No credential handling or CAS code changes. ## Prepared managed-state restoration invariant (not yet verified)
The restoration implementation under preparation replaces the legacy middle-only catch and synthesized development-version rollback. Before controlled production mutations, capture exact bytes, permissions and absence for VERSION, ignore files, root configuration/state and existing root regular files; selected in-project inputs; declared output/docs directory trees; and concrete individual renderer output/asset paths. Capture initially absent parent directories too. Declared external output/docs paths are supported. Raw data, Git internals, arbitrary external user-script effects and cache contents are not backed up. Managed trees containing symlinks or unsupported entries are rejected rather than followed.
Backups use existing tempfile and streaming std::fs copies in private OS temporary recovery storage outside disposable project cache. No project mapping is invented, and cache-free upload-only operations remain supported. Recovery sources are copied to temporary restore staging before any current target is removed. Missing recovery bytes leave intact current state alone and are reported as unavailable.
One local failure boundary covers ignore synchronization, cleanup, all pre/both/ post hooks, engine configuration, execution, output promotion and VERSION writing. Promotion errors propagate; renderer configuration is restored byte-for-byte on success and failure. VERSION changes only after hooks/render/promotion succeed. Failures and caught panics restore captured state. All restore entries are attempted; if restoration fails, retain recovery bytes and report both the original failure and restoration failures with the backup path. Substituted links are rejected.
After local success, storage export/Git publication form a separate failure phase: publication failure reports successful local analysis and retains the new local release. Export precedes requested post-output cleanup so archives contain actual build bytes. A failure during this later cleanup is explicitly reported as such; there is no external publication rollback. No pre-build Git snapshot or second post-build commit is needed. Upstream selection/native credentials and publication retry identity remain separate unfinished work.
Prepared checks cover each hook/analysis failure, initially absent VERSION, exact old output/docs bytes and empty directories, renderer execution/missing promotion, exact YAML comments/render lists, restore-failure backup retention with external sentinels, and successful local analysis followed by failed storage publication. These are unrun: no local compilation under memory pressure; remote CI and independent review are still required. No power-loss atomicity, concurrent-writer or global script-side-effect guarantee is claimed. M2 attempt/release records and analysis-free retry commands remain open.
PR141 review corrections: normalize selected-input identities before comparing root containment (including Windows namespace forms); require nonempty supported document artifacts before project promotion; remove prior expected individual artifacts and project staging immediately before rendering. New regressions cover nested scripts/hooks modifying or deleting themselves, empty renderer staging, stale individual artifacts, cache purge during failed analysis, and unavailable recovery bytes without further deletion. These amendments require fresh remote CI and independent review. Project artifact scanning remains a conservative supported-document check, not a complete renderer manifest guarantee.
Further review keeps project promotion conservative: require a freshly created tree containing a nonempty supported document, rather than guessing per-input filenames from incomplete document-only format metadata. Fake PDF rendering tests cover explicit and inherited project formats. Complete expected-output manifests remain unimplemented; individual document format inference is still a separate known limitation. Selected managed script/hook paths reject symlinks along the original path before canonical identity comparison. System recovery temp anchors are canonicalized, including cache-free operations, without weakening user-path symlink rejection.
Bookdown’s framework-controlled <book_filename>_files source/destination are resolved and guarded before writes, with default _main and portable custom stems. Their exact prior bytes/presence join the recovery set. A fake successful render followed by a failing post-hook checks both default/custom native asset trees and released docs are restored. Unsupported path-like stems fail instead of traversing outside the project. Remote verification and independent review remain required.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:

The same immutable context drives YAML profile selection, clear-output/installation/interaction controls, interpreter dependency probes, scripts/hooks/renderers and existing Git capability/preflight/publication commands. The guarantee is bounded to the build path and commands receiving this context; unrelated external code that concurrently mutates std::env remains outside it. title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different/new, approved root policy: relative to pinned projr 3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d (R/engine.R, R/path.R) and the audited Rust script-parent cwd, scripts/hooks now start in the captured root. Unknown or multiple formats, individual inherited metadata/unsupported output layouts, document-rendering hooks and nested Quarto roots fail early.
