title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different/new: the audited Rust baseline scanned/hash-named files, reopened them for copy, trusted existing objects, normalized Unix literal backslashes into slashes, accepted missing/file sources as empty snapshots and treated manifest existence as verification. This slice rejects missing/non-directory sources and unsafe overlap, linked/unsupported entries, ambiguous logical paths and malformed/non-ASCII digests before unsafe lookup. Literal backslash names are rejected rather than conflated with nested paths. Original source bytes are read only.
Hash the exact stream copied into temporary storage; validate existing object bytes before trusting the digest key. Immutable objects/manifests publish without clobber; manifest conflicts fail instead of truncating existing bytes. Manifest inspection parses/validates JSON and filename hash; file inspection hashes referenced objects. Index replacement uses complete staged bytes with CSV escaping for label/version. Temp fixtures use canonical physical paths so macOS system temp aliases do not silently weaken user-controlled symlink checks.
Ponytail full-mode review reuses BLAKE3, tempfile, shared path guards and standard streaming I/O. No new dependency or CAS schema/version-identity redesign. Prepared remote checks cover malformed paths/digests, Unix backslash collisions, missing/file sources, corrupt existing objects, changed source paths during stream copy, injected read errors, immutable manifest conflict and index failure with old state preserved, CSV metadata escaping and actual referenced-object hashes. Existing empty-directory and dedup/version-sensitive manifest tests remain. Remote CI/review are pending.
This advances existing MiguelRodo/issues#688–690 rather than creating duplicate roadmap issues. Broader CAS lifecycle/GC, a consistent concurrent-source snapshot, multi-writer index updates and crash durability remain open. Failed index publication may leave a complete unindexed manifest; object residue is valid but not a successful indexed export. There is no full cross-filesystem metadata transaction or global scientific reproducibility guarantee. Existing R package remains untouched.
PR145 review adds shared manifest file/directory prefix-collision validation. Logical files a and a/b cannot coexist, independent of input order or intervening names. Both inspection strategies are tested with real digest-matching objects so the rejection proves layout validation, not an unrelated missing-object failure.
CAS metadata readers/writers require regular files before reading existing manifest or index bytes; Unix named-pipe regressions use a bounded completion check so hostile special metadata cannot block verification or ingestion indefinitely.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different/new (approved explicit-action policy): no commit/fetch/push/token requirement is inferred from Git metadata. Omitted commits and not_behind checks are off; explicit actions use the per-run environment. Commit builds fail before writes when Git already contains changes, preserving unrelated work; staged-index no-op is success. Publish one HEAD refspec to the configured current upstream, never origin/main. Custom pushRemote/pushDefault/remote.push routing is conservatively rejected early rather than silently choosing the wrong destination. Local release success remains distinct from publication failure. The retained reference projr and legacy Rust are evidence, not authority for these newer confirmed decisions.
Native Git authentication is default. Explicit use_proj_cred_helper enables only existing single-line environment tokens on standard HTTPS github.com remotes; no build calls GitHub CLI token discovery. Fixed helper code accepts only HTTPS github.com credential requests; the token is quoted environment data, not argv or shell source. The helper list resets for that one command; no persistent config or credentials are created. Captured network failures report status without reflecting potential secret stderr. Other hosts use native configured authentication. See Git’s credential helper protocol and upstream/refspec documentation.
Ponytail full-mode review reuses native Git, existing providers and shared environment context. No new dependency or credential store. Prepared remote checks use fake Git/GH to cover zero implicit calls, configured fetch only, real upstream/refspec, no-op/single commit, dirty-input preservation, native versus opt-in helper behavior, host/protocol denial, punctuation as literal token data, helper reset and secret-free argv/diagnostics. No real network/auth action is tested. Remote CI and independent review are pending; CAS integrity and analysis-free publication retries remain open.
PR143 reviewer note: the shared Windows ASCII assignment restriction also applies to public legacy EnvGuard::track_and_set, not just file-based keys. Inherited native environment values remain preserved; the legacy mutation APIs remain outside the build-path concurrency guarantee.
PR144 review guards force untracked-file and submodule visibility during the clean check, reject pushurl and multiple effective push URLs before writes, and disable follow-tags/submodule recursion for the single explicit push. Extra destinations are also checked at dispatch. Git’s executable is resolved explicitly from the per-run PATH (git.exe on Windows), avoiding native parent-PATH fallback in both availability checks and execution. Remote fixtures cover hidden untracked content, fan-out/redirection rejection and explicit suppression flags. Fresh exact-head checks and independent re-review are required.
The same preflight also rejects mirror pushes, absent remotes, multiple tracking merge entries and effective push/fetch endpoint differences (including expanded pushInsteadOf). Destination inspection uses get-url –push –all before controlled build writes. Native Git configuration is read only; no remote/auth settings are rewritten. Fake regressions assert each unsupported case preserves VERSION and unrelated private bytes and never reaches add/commit/fetch/push.
Captured push identity includes checked-out branch, upstream remote/ref and expanded effective endpoint, without Debug exposure. Revalidate the complete supported identity immediately before commit and again before push. Hook/script changes to URL, pushurl, mirror, branch, ref or remote fail publication without redirecting the push; successful local VERSION/output are retained. Fake regressions switch those values after an analysis marker and assert no add/commit/push occurs. This guards within-run mutation, not an atomic lock against concurrent external Git changes.
The sibling public post_build_sync API now uses the same captured-context checked publication helper as build_project. A fake commit hook changing the endpoint is rejected before push. Explicit Git lookup anchors directories absolutely but preserves the candidate leaf spelling, supporting symlink-based name dispatchers; a fake git-to-dispatcher symlink regression prevents argv[0] canonicalization regressions.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
New: protocol-v1 opt-in JSON envelope and capability version, with static structured failure codes/nonzero exits. Existing human CLI remains default. Queries use explicit-root typed APIs rather than stripping progress prose; config validation returns no raw parameter values. Other command families reuse the existing CLI/domain paths in a noninteractive worker, redirecting child stdout and stderr directly to stderr without log buffering. No credentials/config/argv are copied into protocol errors. User/third-party logs are not auto-redacted.
Pinned projr 3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d is the workflow reference; this machine transport is a new language-neutral boundary, not established R API compatibility. No R code changes, finer domain-error taxonomy, release record or publication-retry semantics. Existing anyhow handling remains the domain layer; issue87 is not duplicated by a cross-module error rewrite.
Ponytail full-mode review uses existing clap/serde/anyhow/query/CLI facilities, standard subprocess stream redirection and no new dependencies. Prepared remote tests cover capability negotiation, typed queries without prose/secrets, malformed config/arguments/root, missing interpreter, child failure/logs, local init and version mutation. CI/independent review pending. Managed preview output isolation remains outstanding and is advertised as false, not described as sandboxing.
PR145 re-cleared CAS head 79050b3a46749a561b5a0cf0cca0451ae5532c6e passed all ten checks and merged 0e10b3e66face673fe966ed61b1be6d2eabf5004; post-merge workflows 39510143656/39510143483/39510143388 passed. CAS multi-writer/crash limits remain as previously recorded.

PR146 review additionally rejects document/format-specific output extension and library-directory overrides before writes; these are outside the modeled artifact and recovery layout. Windows execution-root fixtures compare filesystem identity, preserving the cwd requirement across ordinary/verbatim path spellings.
Effective ancestor Quarto projects are rejected when they differ from an explicitly selected inner proj root. Every selected document routed through Quarto, including Rmd, receives nested-root validation. Metadata traversal normalizes root/input filesystem identity before stopping, avoiding Windows namespace spelling differences.
Retained Markdown (keep_md / keep-md, including format options) is rejected in individual layouts before rendering. A nested Rmd sibling sentinel regression with an overwrite-capable fake renderer and failing post-hook prevents this untracked framework artifact from damaging existing Markdown outside the recovery plan.

title: Future R wrapper: CLI installation and CRAN checks
text:
Status: design direction recorded on 2026-10-20, not a shipped wrapper or an accepted CRAN submission. The existing R package remains untouched. This note does not settle the complete frontend protocol or claim renderer parity.


The future wrapper is intended to contain R code that calls a separately installed proj CLI. Its DESCRIPTION should declare that CLI in SystemRequirements. It should discover a compatible executable and give an actionable missing/incompatible-CLI error. A user-invoked installer on the user’s own machine is distinct from automatic downloads during CRAN installation, checks or examples. Do not assume CRAN servers already provide proj.
CRAN source-package policy permits downloads of precompiled software only as a last resort with CRAN-team agreement. A separate executable is not an automatic exemption. Review Writing R Extensions: portability when implementing the package, including external software availability and portable invocation. This work has neither requested nor obtained CRAN agreement; no outreach is authorized here.










Environment
Required behavior




CRAN, CLI absent
Always run meaningful R-only validation, argument construction, missing-CLI diagnostics and mocked protocol/response tests. Skip only genuine executable integration tests, explicitly because the CLI is unavailable.


CRAN, compatible CLI available
Run the applicable real integration tests as well as the R-only tests. Do not assume every check host supplies it.


Our integration CI
Install an exact pinned CLI release, verify its checksum and compatible version, and run real end-to-end tests. Missing CLI or failed installation is a failure, never a silent skip.



Mocked responses check the wrapper contract; they do not prove the CLI or renderer works. Our mandatory integration job supplies that evidence. Examples and vignettes must also handle optional executable availability honestly instead of requiring an undeclared download. A requirement to execute proj on CRAN check servers would need an agreed deployment/checking arrangement, not an assumed policy exception.



The pinned Quarto R package DESCRIPTION at v1.5.1 declares the separate Quarto command-line tool in SystemRequirements. Its test helper can skip executable-dependent tests when Quarto is unavailable, and its vignette utility checks executable availability during vignette processing. These are specific implementation precedents, not proof that CRAN has accepted a future proj wrapper or guaranteed an executable on every server. This note does not infer automatic binary-download permission from Quarto’s existence.
Before implementation, specify compatible protocol versions, executable discovery, argument quoting, diagnostics, and which tests are unconditional versus executable integration. R production changes require separate authorization.

title: proj yml read
text:
Load and validate configuration without modifying the project:
proj yml read [--project <PATH>]
The command prints a validation confirmation on success and reports configuration errors on stderr. It does not dump configuration values; use proj path get to query a resolved directory path.


The base is _proj.yml, or the legacy alias _projr.yml. Having both is an error. Active _projr-<profile>.yml files override the base, with earlier-listed profiles winning conflicts. _projr-local.yml overrides all active profiles. Explicit profile selection replaces the environment list. Profile/local filename aliases are separate from the implemented base alias.
Read-only queries accept missing configuration as an empty directory inventory. Builds require an active base or explicitly activated profile at the root. Inactive profiles and local overrides alone do not qualify. Every declared directory requires an explicit nonempty path; missing labels are never invented. Unsupported control fields fail validation; metadata and parameters remain arbitrary maps. Parameter aliases normalize before merging; conflicting aliases within one file are rejected. No query writes defaults into configuration.
proj --project . --non-interactive init directories creates a missing base with explicit _raw_data, _tmp and _output paths. It creates declared directories and synchronizes ignore rules without Git/GitHub setup. Existing configuration bytes are preserved. It leaves scripts absent, preserving discovery; scripts: [] continues to mean no analysis.
Configuration validation and path queries do not change .gitignore, .Rbuildignore, configuration files, or project directories. Production builds and directory initialization request ignore synchronization explicitly. Directory initialization stops on configuration read/validation errors before changing ignore rules or creating directories.

title: proj version get
text:
Get the project version based on the VERSION file.


The command searches upwards from the current directory to discover the project root containing the VERSION file. It parses the version text (supporting both raw strings like v1.0.0 or JSON objects) and resolves it to a standard output.
If the VERSION file is missing, the tool attempts to fall back and parse the version from an R package DESCRIPTION file if one is present in the project root. If neither a VERSION file nor a DESCRIPTION file exists, it defaults to a newly initialized v0.0.1.
proj version get





Omits the ‘v’ prefix from the output string.
proj version get --no-v



Specifies the output format: - text (default): Outputs the version as a standard string identifier. - json: Outputs the version as a serialized JSON object, detailing its properties (major, minor, patch, and optionally dev).
proj version get --format json




When using --format=json, the output consists of the separated standard semantic components: - major (integer) - minor (integer) - patch (integer) - dev (integer, optional, indicating build cycles or pre-release versioning)

title: proj path get
text:
Get the resolved absolute path for a given label in the project.
proj path get --label <LABEL> [--project <PATH>]


A label must be declared in the active configuration with a nonempty path. ASCII case is ignored. Undeclared labels and suffixes are errors: declaring raw-data does not declare raw or raw-data-extra. Relative paths resolve against the captured project root; explicit external directories are allowed. Queries do not create directories or route output into a versioned sandbox.



--project PATH selects that exact existing directory, including a folder without configuration or VERSION. It overrides both ancestor discovery and an inherited run root. Invalid directories fail with a nonzero exit status.
The CLI captures an absolute root as PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT for the invocation and its child processes. A nested proj path get uses that root even after a script changes cwd. An invalid inherited root fails rather than falling back silently. Direct Rust build_project(root, ...) calls also pass their supplied root to children. See the discovery rules below for the recognized root markers.
This establishes CLI child-query behavior, not direct Quarto/RStudio parity or changes to the existing R frontend. Renderer configuration, execution cwd, resource links and output placement remain separate concerns. Path queries do not write ignore files or create the resolved target directories.



Without --project or an inherited run root, discovery walks upward from cwd and selects the first recognized directory. It does not search downward for projects. Recognized markers are VERSION, README.md, _quarto.yml, _proj.yml, legacy _projr.yml, Git/SVN metadata, a DESCRIPTION containing Package:, an RStudio .Rproj whose first line starts Version:, and a renv.lock with a Packages map.
pyproject.toml, Project.toml and JuliaProject.toml deliberately extend the projr marker set for Python/Julia. requirements.txt and Manifest.toml alone are not root markers. Standalone VERSION and README markers are retained, so a nested directory with one is the nearer project; explicit selection overrides it.
Marker recognition does not change shallow default script enumeration or prove that the corresponding language runner/frontend is implemented. Legacy config content handling is a separate compatibility change from recognizing its root.
If no recognized marker exists, discovery selects cwd. Discovery success does not mean a build is configured: the current product contract requires active root configuration and explicit used-directory mappings. Validation changes enforcing that newer contract are separate from this root-discovery slice.

title: Install
text:
WarningTry it on a disposable project



Use sample data or a disposable copy of your project. Production builds (proj build) can modify or remove files, and safety fixes are still pending. Never run production builds on the only copy of important work. Previews are not a security sandbox; code you run can still change files.

title: Install
text:
Ubuntu and WSL Ubuntu
Run Linux commands inside Ubuntu, including when Ubuntu runs through WSL. For the first analysis example you need:

The current preview build of projcli, with its source revision recorded.
Python 3, including a python3 command.
A terminal and a writable folder for the example.

Check Python:
python3 --version
The published v0.3.0 release has an amd64.deb asset for Debian-style systems on x86-64 processors. It is a historical package, not the current preview used by this tutorial. No current-preview download command is listed here until the replacement release has been checked.

title: Install
text:
Building from source
This route needs Git, a current stable Rust toolchain with Cargo, and your platform’s C/C++ linker tools. The crate uses Rust’s 2024 edition. Ubuntu commonly supplies the linker tools through build-essential.
The source-install command below was verified on Ubuntu in CI on 20 October 2026. That run installed source revision fafce46a and ran both documented examples through the CLI:
cargo install --git https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli --locked --bin proj
This command installs the current repository source, which can change after that check. It does not install the historical release package.
Cargo normally places the command in ~/.cargo/bin; that folder must be on your PATH. Record the installed commit from Cargo’s output when trying a development build. The version number alone does not identify the recent features.

title: Install
text:
Check which command you have
Another program can also use the name proj. In Ubuntu, check both its location and its help:
command -v proj
proj --help
For this project’s current preview, help lists build-dev, --project and --non-interactive. If those are missing, check which executable your shell found before continuing.

title: Install
text:
Other systems
Windows amd64 builds are exercised in CI. A released native Windows installer has not yet been verified for the current preview. Published macOS and ARM binary assets have not been established either. Rust test coverage on a platform does not establish that a release installer works there.

title: Install
section: Extra tools depend on your project
text:
Extra tools depend on your project
The first tutorial uses only Python’s standard library. R scripts need R and Rscript; reports may additionally need Quarto, rmarkdown or bookdown. Install the tools required by your own targets before running them. Git and remote credentials are needed only for workflows that use those integrations.
